note: The ARMING law of the self-dispatched flowEvalTick chain, declared as data. `🪟️tick-addressing.json` says WHICH window an armed tick names; this says WHETHER one may be armed at all. The invariant every row proves: at most ONE pending flowEvalTick per (app instance, preview window) exists at any time, no matter how many independent sources ask for one — the host refresh poll, a contributions install, an example switch, a view command, and the chain's own continuations all pass through the retained FlowEvalSession's per-window latch. Language-agnostic: an implementation in any language must replay these event sequences and answer the same `armed` lists.

events.refresh: One host refreshUi pass asks the app for pending effects. Arms a window only while that window OWES a tick nothing else is chasing.
events.gesture: A command that changed what the evaluation would produce (setContributions after the registry moved, setActiveExample, a generation command, a viewer view command). Arms every attached preview — through the latch, so a window that already owes a tick gets no second one.
events.tick: The armed tick RUNS on the named window. `parks` is how many ExtensionInvocations it declared; `more` is whether the evaluation is unfinished. A tick that parked work owes no re-arm: its answers own the continuation.
events.resolve: One extension answer comes back for the named window. `ok` is whether it could be folded into the session (a faulted invokeExtension folds nothing); `more` is whether the fold left work behind.
events.invalidate: The flow extension registry was replaced, so every result the old chain was chasing has been swept and every window's latch is abandoned.
events.detach: A refresh pass ran while the named window was NOT in the shell's roster. Its latch can never be discharged by a tick once it is gone, so that pass drops it and the window owes a first tick again when it comes back.

rows.why: Each preview window owns its own retained evaluation publication, so the install owes each one a chain — and owes each exactly one.
The poll used to run on a throwaway session whose latch was always clear, so every refresh stacked another tick on the running chain.
A window that has never ticked owes its first one; after that the latch holds until the tick actually runs.
Ticking a window whose invocation is outstanding recomputes the identical pending request and parks a duplicate — the 298-invocations-against-111-settles spin.
The answer owns the continuation the tick that parked it declined to owe.
A budgeted tessellation parks one invocation per handle; the LAST answer arms the next tick, the earlier ones hand their claim on.
A faulted invokeExtension folds nothing, so the next tick would park the identical request and fault again at the host's own cadence. Only a gesture may resume it.
Idle turns cost nothing: a finished evaluation owes no continuation and the poll asks the latch, not an evaluation.
A graph that outruns one step budget continues itself, and the poll must not add a second chain on top of it.
Generate-mode previews evaluate a patched fixture of their own, so a window's debt is that window's, never the session's.
A detached window's armed latch can never be discharged — the retained route refuses a window that has left the roster — so a stale latch would make it unarmable forever.
The viewer runs the identical shared chain; two gestures in a row still leave one pending tick.
One answer asking for a continuation is enough; the last answer of the fan-out carries it.
